title: Is It a Person or a Computer? Experts Share Tips on Young Kids and AI
summary:
Young children are meeting artificial intelligence, or AI, in their everyday lives. They hear smart assistants like Amazon's Alexa or Apple's Siri at home, and they may see AI-made videos on YouTube. Experts say the years before age 8 are an important time to help kids understand what AI is and what it is not.

Lauren Girouard, a researcher at the Harvard Graduate School of Education and the University of Michigan, studies how children 12 and under use digital information. She said preschoolers can already learn from technology. She added that AI learning tutors can be valuable, but researchers are still learning how kids interact with the AI tools many families have used at home since ChatGPT arrived at the end of 2022.

Jennifer Katzenstein of Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital suggested that when a smart speaker answers, parents can explain, "That's the computer answering." She also said kids can ask another adult what they think, so they learn the difference between a human answer and a computer answer.

Dr. Jenny Radesky of the University of Michigan said little kids are "much more magical thinkers." Until her son was 7, he thought Siri was a real woman living in California. She suggested reminding kids that a machine has never felt sad and does not have a body. She also suggested giving a smart speaker a wake word that is not a human name, such as "Computer."

Dr. Molly O'Shea, a pediatrician, said parents can also skip smart devices. When a child asks a question the parent cannot answer, they can guess and solve the problem out loud together.

Common Sense Media, a group that studies the risks of tech products, has urged parents to keep AI toys away from children 5 and younger.
why_it_matters: As AI tools become part of everyday family life, helping young children tell the difference between people and machines may shape how they trust and learn from technology.

keywords.explanation: Artificial intelligence is computer technology that can do tasks that usually need human thinking, like answering questions.
Smart assistants are voice programs, like Alexa or Siri, that answer questions and follow spoken commands.
Preschoolers are young children, usually ages 3 to 5, who are not yet in kindergarten.
Tutors are helpers who teach one student or a small group, and some are now computer programs.
A wake word is the word you say to make a smart speaker start listening.
A pediatrician is a doctor who takes care of children.

background_read: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is computer technology that can answer questions, tell stories or make content in ways that can seem human.
Smart assistants like Alexa and Siri listen for a wake word and then answer out loud, which is why young children may think a real person is talking.
Many families have used personal AI tools at home since ChatGPT arrived at the end of 2022, so researchers are still studying how these tools affect young kids.
Experts focus on the years before age 8 because a lot of important brain development happens then.

Little kids are magical thinkers, so parents should explain in concrete terms that AI is not human.
